request.summary: Cockpit V2 (C01, roadmap A7): a cockpit Benjamin can trust and act from, with ntfy phone notifications, ritual reminders and per-project progress, replacing the interim NEEDS BENJAMIN / proposal / ritual lines at operator session start.

shared_understanding.statement: Intent: Benjamin, SayMyName decisions 6 (2026-09-25, ntfy need kept: « Je veux continuer à avoir un système de notifications ntfy. Mais son utilisation devra être revue en même temps que le cockpit »), 11 (ritual reminders become notifications), 18 (NEEDS BENJAMIN list and proposal count move from session start into the cockpit) and 23 (C01 before B1; its 'publish after A6 closes' part amended in round 5). Grilled with the PO on 2026-09-29 in four rounds (Q1-Q26 plus the kanban discussion); exact answers in decisions-log.md; recap confirmed « Q24 à Q26 ok, lance le router ». A first Spec (sha256:fada0d2e…) was approved, then amended in round 5 (publish now; UI/UX gate) after Benjamin's questions « pourquoi absolument attendre A6 » and « est ce que l'UI UX est pris en compte » and his answer « A oui, B oui ».

Inputs: proposals af-sqrri (duplicate notification bursts) and af-pgm3y (stale re-fires); facts.md (2026-09-29, live read-only); the night of 2026-09-28/29 (worker loops, Mayor idle, test-mail leaks, silent failures); Cockpit V1 and old ntfy code in legacy/ read as evidence only, never reused as trusted code.
Why Cockpit V1 failed becomes this run's acceptance: it was noisy, unreliable, had stale sections, did not say what to do, and Benjamin had to ask an agent to understand it (Q2).
Push first and a dashboard he can trust, on one screen: the phone tells Benjamin when he is needed; the cockpit says what waits for him, why, and what to do, and shows project progress (Q3).
af-sqrri and af-pgm3y are delivered by this run and closed with it (Q1).
No quiet hours in the Factory: notifications are sent at any hour; Benjamin's phone settings decide whether they make noise (Q5).

Benjamin can act without an agent, every action leaving a trace, and can continue with an agent without friction (Q6). Allowed without an agent: acknowledge or snooze an alert; answer a NEEDS BENJAMIN decision when the escalating agent prepared options; accept, reject with a reason, or defer a proposal; resume a session or order the Factory paused. Not without an agent: approving a Spec or a ticket graph, and anything owner-tier (spend, exposure, irreversible) (Q10).
'Continue with an agent' copies a provider-neutral ready prompt (what happens, ids, the open question) usable with Codex or Claude; launching an agent session directly is out of this run (Q11).

The Factory stays project-agnostic and agent-provider-agnostic. Project information comes from a project manifest kept in each project's own repository (name, code repos, roadmap file, state file, display language); the Factory holds only a pointer per project; the Factory has its own manifest (Q7, Q12).
One roadmap: the SayMyName roadmap (which holds the Factory's A steps) is the only roadmap shown; the Factory's card shows its convoys, kanban and health, not a roadmap of its own (Q24).

Reachable from the PC and the iPhone through Tailscale only (Benjamin's private network); nothing public, no Tailscale Funnel (Q9). Only localhost and tailnet requests are served; the Tailscale identity (account and device) is written in every action trace; no extra code or password (Q20).

The first delivery slice is a vertical slice that includes the phone (PO choice delegated by Benjamin: « je te laisse choisir »), because the risky unknowns are mobile: iOS push latency and Tailscale serving the page.
ntfy through hosted ntfy.sh, free, with a new secret topic (not the V1 one) kept out of git and never printed; no spend (Q13).
Zero model tokens: the cockpit, the notifier and the watcher are pure code; only an agent session Benjamin chooses to open spends tokens (Q19).
The cockpit adds no new escalation ladder; it surfaces the existing one (Mayor first, NEEDS BENJAMIN after 2 h, third PR rejection) (Q18).

Kanban option a: a read-only kanban per project; ticket display titles in the operator's language are provided by planning as a field of the ticket graph, never translated at display time (Q22 discussion: « a, avec titres français fournis par la planification »).

Session start loses the NEEDS BENJAMIN list, the proposal count and the ritual line, each only after its cockpit replacement is proven (Q21). The interim line added on 2026-09-29 to SayMyName AGENTS.md (escalation-door list) is removed then (Q16).

The graph is published as soon as Benjamin approves it, without waiting for A6 to close (amends SayMyName decision 23; round 5 « A oui »): A6's workers are idle after its last batch, so C01 gives P22's 24 h window real parallel work. Accepted consequence: if a C01 merge breaks main or makes an order fail, P22's window restarts.

UI/UX gate (round 5 « B oui »): before any ticket that renders the cockpit UI, a throwaway clickable prototype (home in three zones, a project page with the kanban, answering an option; synthetic data) is made by the PO with Benjamin and approved by him on PC and iPhone; it fixes the visual baseline (typography, colours, spacing, dark mode). Every UI ticket shows phone-width and desktop-width screenshots in its PR; the reviewer compares them with the approved prototype and escalates any visible deviation.

General rule for every project (class fix: SayMyName's showcase site was delivered with no prototype, no design baseline and no visual acceptance): a ticket that renders UI declares it in the ticket graph and must have an operator-approved prototype ticket among its blockers, and its PR carries phone-width and desktop-width screenshots checked by the reviewer against the prototype (round 5 « B oui »).

Reliability: the cockpit stores no copy of Factory state. Each block re-reads its live source (Beads, GitHub, gc events, project files) when shown and displays its source and check time (Paris); if a source fails it shows 'unknown: <source> unreachable', never an older value. No hand-written section exists that could go stale (Q8).

Home screen in three zones: (1) 'What waits for you' — only items needing Benjamin's action, or an explicit 'nothing waits for you, checked HH:MM'; (2) 'Project progress' — one card per project: current roadmap step, current convoy progress (done/total, what runs, earliest end), blocked or not; (3) 'Factory health' — one line, 'normal' or the plain statement of what is not. A condition appears once (same dedup key as notifications); resolved items leave the home screen for a journal page; technical details are folded and open on demand; nothing is shown that answers neither 'what must I do' nor 'where are we' (Q14, Q17).

Every item reads: what, why it waits for you, what to do (action buttons), in plain language of the operator's configured language (French for Benjamin); ids and codes appear only in folded details, never alone (Q15).

Notification levels (Q4, Q18). Urgent: a new NEEDS BENJAMIN item (including a Mayor-first escalation promoted after 2 h and a third PR rejection); the Factory stopped (controller down, all providers exhausted, factory-guard failing repeatedly); a loop detected and paused whose resume belongs to Benjamin. Normal: a ticket graph delivered, a proof window passed or broken, a ritual becoming due. Not on the phone (cockpit only): new proposals (count and list), a red PR, an isolated order.failed, an idle Mayor and other conditions agents handle themselves, shown in Factory health only if they persist.

Anti-noise rule for notifications: one notification when a condition starts; nothing while it stays open (no periodic reminder); a new one only if its level rises or it recurs after being resolved; a 'resolved' notification only for urgent conditions; no digest. Conditions are keyed so that the bursts of af-sqrri and the stale re-fires of af-pgm3y produce one notification or none (Q14).
Notification payload: level, event class, project and a link to the cockpit item; never bead bodies, free text from agents, product data or any real person's data (SayMyName real-person-data rule).

Actions without an agent (Q10) are executed through the Factory's existing doors (escalation door, dispatch/resume doors, proposal handling), never by direct state edits; each writes a trace naming Benjamin, 'via cockpit', the Tailscale device and the Paris time, both in the bead and in gc events. A NEEDS BENJAMIN item without prepared options offers only 'continue with an agent'.
Escalations that reach Benjamin carry prepared options when the escalating agent can state them (a/b/c plus 'other → agent'), so the cockpit can offer them as buttons.

Project pages: from a project card, a page shows the project's roadmap (steps done / in progress / next, read from the manifest's roadmap file), a read-only kanban of the current ticket graph (columns: to do — ready or waiting on another ticket; in progress — with who works on it; in PR — with CI state; done — with the merged PR link), and previous graphs folded as history. Only approved-graph tickets, bugs and proposals appear, never molecules, steps, mails or wisps. A card shows the display title, why the ticket exists (link to the Spec), its live state and GitHub links. No drag and drop, no editing (Q22).

Ticket graph drafts carry, per ticket, a display title in the operator's language; ticket-graph-publish keeps it on the published bead; the kanban falls back to the original title, marked as such, when a graph predates the field.

Rituals: when a ritual becomes due (rituals-status rule of the project), one normal notification and an item in 'What waits for you' with 'run with an agent' (ready prompt) and 'postpone' (traced). Rituals are still run only by Benjamin's choice (decision 11).

Watcher: a small pure-code watcher on the Windows host checks a Factory heartbeat; after 30 minutes without it, it sends one urgent 'Factory silent since HH:MM' notification and one 'Factory back' notification when the heartbeat returns; no repetition in between. PC off means nothing is sent (Q25).

Host-side steps are done by Benjamin, guided step by step, at the mobile slice: installing or checking the ntfy app and subscribing to the new topic, keeping Tailscale connected on the iPhone, enabling `tailscale serve` on Windows for the tailnet only (never `funnel`), and installing the Windows watcher's scheduled task. No ticket changes host or network settings itself (Q26).

The SayMyName project manifest lives in the SayMyName project repo, which is not a Factory rig: the PO writes it there; Factory tickets define the manifest format, the pointer and the Factory's own manifest only.
No ticket reuses legacy/ code as trusted code; legacy/ may only be read as evidence.
Session-start lines (SayMyName AGENTS.md: rituals and escalation-door list) are removed only after their replacement is proven; the removal in the SayMyName repo is done by the PO, not by a worker.

Mobile slice: a synthetic NEEDS BENJAMIN item with prepared options produces one ntfy notification on the iPhone; tapping it opens the cockpit item over Tailscale; answering an option executes through the escalation door and writes the trace (Benjamin, via cockpit, device, Paris time) in the bead and in gc events.
The prototype is approved by Benjamin in the live chat (quoted with its date) before any UI ticket starts; each UI ticket's PR shows phone-width and desktop-width screenshots matching it.
Test: ticket-graph-publish refuses a draft in which a ticket declared as rendering UI has no approved prototype ticket among its blockers.
Test: each cockpit block compared with its live source shows the same facts; with a source made unreachable the block shows 'unknown', never an older value.

Replay of the recorded events of the night of 2026-09-28/29 (and the af-sqrri / af-pgm3y cases) through the notifier and the home screen: zero duplicate notification, no stale item, a home screen of a few lines.
Test: a notification payload never contains bead bodies or agent free text; a fixture with a person-like name in a bead body never reaches the payload.
Test: requests from outside localhost and the tailnet are refused; every accepted action records the Tailscale identity.
Test: a synthetic third project declared only through its manifest appears with its card, roadmap and kanban without any Factory code naming it.
Test: the watcher sends exactly one 'silent' and one 'back' notification across a faked 45-minute heartbeat gap.
No model call anywhere in the cockpit, notifier or watcher code paths (checked by test or static check).

Final proof (A7 done): the graph delivered and closed, then 3 days of real use in which every NEEDS BENJAMIN item reached the phone, zero duplicate notification, zero false or stale screen line (checked against sources), and Benjamin declares he did not need to ask an agent 'where are we' (Q23).
Measure the delay between a condition and the iOS notification during the mobile slice and the 3-day proof; report it in the closing note.

Count, during the 3-day proof, home-screen lines per day and the actions taken without an agent vs through 'continue with an agent'; input for a later decision on kanban actions (option b) or direct agent launch.
The cockpit does not replace GitHub or Beads: no ticket editing, commenting, code review or full history search; it links out (Q22).
No kanban actions (drag and drop, reprioritising), no Spec or graph approval from the cockpit, no product metrics or user data, one user only (Benjamin), no public page, no paid service (Q22, Q13).
No direct launch of an agent session from the cockpit; no digest; no quiet hours; no translation at display time.
